title: useRef — what is it
question: What is the `useRef` hook in React and what are its two main use cases?
realWorldScenario: 1. Accessing a DOM element directly (focus input on mount). 2. Storing a mutable value that doesn't cause re-renders (interval ID, previous value).

title: useRef vs useState
question: When should you use `useRef` instead of `useState` to store a value in React?
seoKeywords: when to use useRef instead of useState
realWorldScenario: Storing a setInterval ID — you need to access it in cleanup but changing it shouldn't cause a re-render.

title: useMemo hook
question: What does `useMemo` do in React and when should you use it?
realWorldScenario: Filtering a 10,000-item list based on a search input — `useMemo` ensures the filter runs only when the list or search term changes, not every render.

title: useCallback hook
question: What does `useCallback` do in React and when is it useful?
realWorldScenario: A parent passes `handleClick` to a memoized child — without `useCallback`, the function is recreated every render, making React.memo useless.

title: useMemo vs useCallback
question: What is the difference between `useMemo` and `useCallback`?
searchIntent: when to use useMemo vs useCallback
realWorldScenario: `useMemo(() => fn(), deps)` caches the return value of fn; `useCallback(fn, deps)` caches the fn itself.

title: When NOT to use useMemo/useCallback
question: When should you NOT use `useMemo` or `useCallback` in React?
seoKeywords: when not to use useMemo react
searchIntent: when not to use useMemo useCallback react
realWorldScenario: Wrapping every function and value in memo hooks adds overhead without benefit when the computation is trivial. Profile first, memoize second.

title: React.memo
question: What is `React.memo` and how does it work with `useCallback`?
realWorldScenario: `React.memo` prevents a child from re-rendering when props are shallowly equal — but only works with useCallback for function props.
